name: fireside
description: Drop in an EPUB or paste a public story link and fireside narrates it, chapter by chapter. Built for long serialized fiction: no subscription wall, no account required, runs on your own machine. Bring your own TTS key (Azure, OpenAI-compatible, MiniMax) or point it at a local engine such as Kokoro and it costs nothing per word. Open source (MIT). • EPUB, pasted story links, and Archive of Our Own (with optional login cookie) • Per-chapter audio you can replay, plus continuous "whole book" mode • Local filesystem storage by default; SQLite metadata by default, MySQL/MariaDB optional • Character-capacity accounting hooks for hosted use; self-host is free First run: open the WebUI, add a speech engine on the Settings page, drop in a book, and press play.

paths.name: Data
paths.description: Library metadata and content-addressed audio blobs. Point this at appdata so your library survives container updates. Ownership is handled for you: the container makes this directory writable by its app user on start, so a root-owned appdata path will not stop it from booting. Set PUID/PGID below if you want the files owned by a specific user instead.

ports.name: WebUI Port
ports.description: Port for the fireside WebUI and API.

variables.name: Data Dir
variables.description: Where the host keeps its state inside the container. Leave as /data unless you changed the path above.

variables.name: Database Engine
variables.description: sqlite (default, zero setup) or mysql. Leave this as sqlite and fireside keeps its metadata in a file under the Data path. Nothing else to do. Set it to mysql to move metadata (accounts, books, chapters, connections) to an external MySQL/MariaDB server, then fill in Database Connection below. Audio blobs stay under the Data path either way.

variables.name: Database Connection
variables.description: Only used when Database Engine is mysql. Form: user:password@host:3306/dbname (a full mysql:// DSN also works). Example: fireside:secret@192.168.1.10:3306/fireside The database and user must exist first. In the MySQL server run: CREATE DATABASE fireside CHARACTER SET utf8mb4; CREATE USER 'fireside'@'%' IDENTIFIED BY 'secret'; GRANT ALL ON fireside.* TO 'fireside'@'%'; Fireside creates its own tables on first start.

variables.name: Plugins Root
variables.description: Directory the host scans for reader/speech/storage plugins. Leave default unless you mount a custom plugin set.

variables.name: PUID
variables.description: Owner of the files fireside writes under the Data path. Leave default unless you want them owned by a specific user; the container applies this on start.

variables.name: PGID
variables.description: Group of the files fireside writes under the Data path. Leave default unless you want them owned by a specific group; the container applies this on start.
